summary: Sensor fusion, data fusion, dashboards and data visualisation are conventionally distinguished by input type and by where they sit in a processing stack. This paper argues that the distinction which matters for decision quality is a different one, and that it is two variables applied to all four: every representation of multi-source evidence collapses a distribution somewhere between sensor and decision, and representations differ in the locus of that collapse and in whether the residual uncertainty survives it as a carried object. Fusion collapses upstream and, when honest, ships the residual as covariance or hypothesis mass. Dashboards defer collapse to the viewer's retina and ship nothing; the resulting belief has no bookkeeping. Visualisation is the encoding of whichever object arrives, indifferent to whether it is a point or a distribution, which is why it is blamed for collapses committed upstream. The two variables, collapse locus and residual retention, place the four terms on one map, generalise the confabulation coefficient of The Confabulating Collator from language-model collators to the whole representation stack, and yield a diagnostic: the failure mode conventionally called bad fusion is a product that collapsed upstream and discarded its residual, delivering the confidence of a posterior with the epistemic hygiene of a gauge. The publicly reported expectation, in the investigation of the February 2026 Minab strike, that a targeting platform would have flagged contradictions it carried no representation of, is read as this failure at operational scale, with the causal question left where the public record leaves it. A design rule follows: defer collapse to the human where the human carries the prior the system lacks, fuse where they do not, and at neither locus discard the residual. The constructive requirement for language-level fusion products is stated and handed to a companion paper on divergence retention. The operator located in the architecture is Binary Bias.

summary: The Admiralty Code, the two-axis grading of source reliability (A to F) and information credibility (1 to 6) carried in NATO intelligence doctrine, grades the inputs to analysis. It has no address for the analyst's own inferences, in particular the identification and linkage judgements that decide which reports concern the same person, object, or event, and its top credibility grade presumes an independence between confirming sources that the evaluator has no field to check. This paper argues that both gaps are structural, and that a closed historical archive exposes them more cleanly than live intelligence work, because an archive cannot be re-tasked. Using a worked example of invented but plausible fifteenth-century English borough-court, ale-assize, and probate entries, it proposes four repairs. First, a third axis for link hypotheses, built as a ladder of work rather than a scale of feeling: seven rungs from 0 (admissible) through 1 (hunch) to 6 (closed by record), each defined by an inquiry step completed, so that every grade also names the next task. Second, a production-lineage field that reserves both the top credibility grade and the convergent rung of the ladder for confirmation across distinct lineages, naming the failure it prevents genlyd: corroboration that is the same voice returned. Third, aggregation over possible readings with an explicit sensitivity sweep, so that ordinal grades never silently become probabilities, every conclusion carries a robustness verdict, and the links can be ranked into a work plan by how much each moves the conclusions. Fourth, the paper turns the ladder back on the code itself, arguing that the existing grades should travel with a work rung beside them rather than be replaced, and that divergence between grade and work is a diagnostic signal in its own right. The proposal is offered both to intelligence doctrine and to digital prosopography, and six falsifiable predictions are stated for analyst training.

summary: Binary Bias (Temte 2026a) claims that the collapse of continuous, conditional and multi-valued phenomena into sealed either/or categories is a substrate from which other catalogued biases grow. The claim has so far been argued, not counted. This paper specifies an audit that counts it: a random sample of 3,000 journal-article abstracts drawn through Crossref's sampling endpoint, enriched with field and era metadata from OpenAlex, and coded for binary collapse by three independent language-model coders with ten percent human double-coding. The coding scheme separates four loci at which a binary can sit (territory, design, inference, format), scores severity on a 0 to 5 Boolikert rather than as present or absent, and counts the sealing of a null result into an absence claim (nulsegl) as its own category. An evening-scale pilot of twenty abstracts, reported in full, motivates six hypotheses with pre-stated effect sizes: that inference- and format-locus collapse appears in at least a quarter of abstracts; that the format locus dominates in clinical literature and the inference locus in social and policy literature; that nulsegl is the single most frequent collapse type; that fields whose core object is already a ratio collapse less than fields whose core object is a category; that the 2016 statement on p-values changed vocabulary rather than verdicts; and that abstracts collapse more than the discussion sections they summarise. Publication of the protocol before the data is the pre-registration; the result is published whichever way it falls.

summary: Validation dataset of the H5MD biophysics module, a metadata schema that stores the topology, force field, MD parameters, selection groups and observables of a molecular dynamics simulation together with its trajectory in one H5MD (HDF5) file. It accompanies the paper A Hierarchical Metadata Schema for Self-Contained Molecular Dynamics Trajectory Archives . validation_systems.zip contains the GROMACS inputs of the 58 chemical systems used in the paper's technical validation, reduced to what grompp needs: topology, force field, coordinates or run input, index groups and MD parameters. The systems range from 711 to 1,066,628 particles, cover AMBER, CHARMM, GROMOS, OPLS-AA and MARTINI force fields, and come in six groups by origin: self_generated (8): built with GROMACS from PDB entries bena (10): sessions of the Bena dataset ( 10.5281/zenodo.17632513 ) jcp_benchmark (6): GROMACS benchmark systems ( 10.5281/zenodo.3893789 ) hexabc (8): hexABC nucleic-acid and protein–nucleic-acid deposits from MDposit memprotmd (6): MemProtMD membrane proteins, atomistic and coarse-grained misato (20): MISATO protein–ligand complexes ( 10.5281/zenodo.7711953 ) Run under 23 simulation protocols, these inputs give the 379 reference files of the validation. The files can be regenerated with the validation scripts ( github.com/miemiemmmm/h5md-biophysics-validation ) and the GROMACS implementation published with the paper. Each group's MANIFEST.md credits its source and states the changes made; provenance/ holds the scripts that selected and prepared the systems. Four of the reference files are included as examples, each a short trajectory with the full metadata. They also serve as test data for the validator in gitlab.com/gromacs/h5md-biophysics : hexabc_a001u2_rna_protein__nvt-vrescale.h5md bench_villin__tcoupl-multigroup.h5md bench_villin__sd-langevin.h5md bench_villin__selection-noncontiguous.h5md

summary: A shibboleth economy is a cultural system in which the rewards of decoding, a fluency-gain reward, identity affirmation, collective affiliation, and positional rank, become self-sustaining, so that demand for distinction feeds back into cultural production and communicative opacity becomes value-bearing rather than merely costly. Cultural capital theory, from Bourdieu through the fan-studies lineage, explains why scarce decoding competence produces distinction; a shibboleth economy begins where that distinction becomes demand and the demand alters what gets made, through evolutionary selection on engagement rather than any calculating producer. The paper develops the loop and its consequences. A two-type model distinguishes lexical figuration, which maps represented features to meanings and is bootstrappable within a single work, from modal figuration, which maps the representational act itself to an ontological status and is stabilised only by shared representational infrastructure, of which canon is the most powerful form. In markets poor in effective codebook coverage, exemplified by industrial-era Hollywood, uncaught references are priced as lost customers and a self-teaching visual pidgin is selected, later mistaken for neutral realism; in codebook-rich markets the operating point moves to selective permeability, legible to the invested and closed to the casual, with the equilibrium set by the opposed pulls of affiliation and rank. Democratisation of a key causes migration and displacement rather than collapse; a hard cultural border is a boundary condition that slows depreciation and opens an export axis; and when demand for keys outruns authenticated supply, the predicted pathology is key inflation, defined as growth in the ratio of claimed authorised readings to verifiably authorised ones, driven by provenance laundering. Two model-implied expectations, codebook import markets and synthetic canon manufacture, are tested against known cases, with modal transfer breadth as the surviving strong claim, and three forward predictions are stated, led by key migration under democratisation.
